title: Open-site cohomology comparisons and Zariski vanishing detection
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $T_\tau$ either its small etale or its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using small representatives in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A_T$ denote the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_\tau,A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^a$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be any set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$.
For every open $U\subseteq T$, the functor $(V\to U)\mapsto(V\to T,V\to U)$ identifies $U_\tau$ with the localized site $T_\tau/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], including its topology. Under this identification there is a canonical ring isomorphism $A_U\cong A_T|_U$, the identity on constant sections, and restriction of module sheaves is the exact sectionwise functor $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V\to T)$. These identifications respect iterated open restriction. The family $(U_i\to T)$ is a cover on $T_\tau$, and for every object $V\to T$ its pullback $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$ is a cover on $V_\tau$ and on the corresponding localized site.
Writing $r_U$ for this exact restriction and $D(r_U)$ for its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], there are canonical isomorphisms
$$\chi^a_{U,K}:r_U\mathcal H^a(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^a(D(r_U)K)$$
for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(T_\tau,A)$. They are induced by the kernel, image and quotient comparisons, are natural for all derived morphisms, and agree with the composite comparisons for nested opens. For every module sheaf $F$ one has $F=0$ if and only if $r_{U_i}F=0$ for every $i$. Consequently, for every integer $a$,
$$\mathcal H^a(K)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathcal H^a(D(r_{U_i})K)=0\text{ for every }i.$$
These assertions include $T=\varnothing$ and the empty covering family; in that case every module sheaf is zero.
